rejected_detail.title: Harness stats-stream write failure is logged but never affects the exit code
rejected_detail.reason: Spec-compliant by the committed I/O matrix: harness row says 'unwritable path -> logged failure (never silent)'; the exit-1 contract is scoped to the APP row only (app implements it). eprintln satisfies never-silent.

rejected_detail.title: PP_DEBUG overlay builds every per-frame label with default-allocator fmt.tprintf — unreclaimed heap growth
rejected_detail.reason: Falsified by the Odin stdlib: fmt.tprintf allocates via context.temp_allocator (core/fmt/fmt.odin:230-233). The labels die with the frame via the new per-frame free_all — the r3 fmt_tmp->tprintf change is behavior-identical (fmt_tmp was a tprintf pass-through) and now properly reclaimed.

rejected_detail.title: demo_destroy comment claims extraction 'from the three inlined copies' but only one call site converted
rejected_detail.reason: Two call sites use demo_destroy (run_demo run.odin:233, overlay_check overlay.odin:39 — both in this diff). The third historical inline site (load_demo_replay) intentionally keeps a partial teardown because string ownership transfers to Demo_Replay — documented at demo_destroy itself ('NOT for Demo_Replay ... owns its own partial teardown').

findings.title: App silently ignores the --stats-out=<path> equals form (and any unrecognized token) — telemetry-off with exit 0, no diagnostic
findings.evidence: for i := 1; i < len(os.args); i += 1 { if os.args[i] == "--stats-out" { ... } } — exact-token match only; no else/unknown-arg branch; app.stats_live = stats_path != "". `app --stats-out=x` leaves stats_path empty and the app runs green with no stream.
findings.detail: Same silent-telemetry-off family as r2-W3 (fixed for the empty token this round): an unsupported-but-plausible syntax bypasses the guard. Harness treats the token as a demo name (fails loud); the app ignores it.
findings.recommended_fix: In the app parser, reject any argv token starting with '-' that is not the exact two-token form (usage error, exit 2).

findings.title: Committed spec's AC4 mechanism text ('harness builds never pass -define:PP_DEBUG'; 'Release + harness builds carry ZERO overlay code') is contradicted by this round's own CI harness PP_DEBUG build
findings.evidence: spec: 'harness builds never pass `-define:PP_DEBUG`'; ci.yml (new in r3): 'odin build harness -define:PP_DEBUG=true -out:bin/harness-debug'.
findings.detail: The R2-W2 CI gate (compile-only; never runs goldens) breaks the spec's absolute wording. Golden safety itself is intact (25/25 byte-identical; plain build runs goldens) — the contract text is now stale/misleading.
findings.recommended_fix: One-line spec edit: the GOLDEN path never builds with PP_DEBUG; the CI compile gate builds a separate debug artifact that never runs goldens.

findings.title: R2-W4 residual: the app's per-frame free_all vs stream/record lifetime is verified by code-reading only — no automated test exercises the app loop
findings.evidence: free_all(context.temp_allocator) per frame; stats_sb builder_make(context.allocator); stats_emit default allocator = context.allocator (core/stats.odin:265); catalogs' json strings cloned into the general allocator (encoding/json clone_string). GUI loop is not unit-testable as-is.

findings.recommended_fix: Optional: a comment in stats_emit pinning the 'record must outlive the caller's frame' allocator contract.

findings.title: R2-N9 residual: the CSV header legend lines (6 '#' comment rows) are not pinned string-for-string — a legend drift passes all tests
findings.evidence: test_stats_csv_literal_rows calls stats_write_header(&sb) but asserts only the G/C/P/D row literals, not the header output.
findings.detail: Legend is documentation (comment rows); data literals are pinned. A legend edit that misdocuments a column passes silently.

findings.title: Paused-wall-ticks-emit-no-rows has no discriminating pin — a symmetric both-driver regression (emitting on un-stepped ticks) stays byte-identical
findings.detail: Per-stepped-tick semantics are enforced by construction in both drivers (emit lives inside the step loop); no test pins row-count == stepped-tick-count directly.
findings.recommended_fix: Optional: assert stream G-row count == final tick for a pause-schedule demo.

findings.title: Spec says 'per-frame stats compute when the overlay is on'; the code computes per STEPPED tick only (paused frames re-display the last record)
findings.evidence: spec: 'per-stepped-tick stats append (stream) + per-frame stats compute when the overlay is on'; code: stats_emit inside the step loop, gated if app.stats_live || app.overlay_on.
findings.detail: The deviation is the safer semantics blessed in r1/r2 (a paused frame never fabricates a record; state frozen = display frozen). Spec wording is loose.
findings.recommended_fix: Align the spec wording to per-stepped-tick for both stream and overlay record.

findings.title: App stats builder is allocated + header-written unconditionally but deleted only when stats_live — the off-path builder buffer is never freed (exit-time, constant-size)
findings.evidence: app.stats_sb = strings.builder_make(context.allocator); pp.stats_write_header(&app.stats_sb); defer if app.stats_live { ...; delete(...) } — no else-branch delete.
findings.detail: One constant header (~300 B) per process, reclaimed by OS exit. Cosmetic asymmetry only.
findings.recommended_fix: Optional: delete the builder unconditionally in the defer.
